clue.text: A politician in retreat — so wet!

indicators.note: the politician with the article sits inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or hideaway
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how feeble a withdrawing politician is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so wet!' reads as a jibe at a feeble politician (British 'wet' = weak), but 'wet' is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something slightly is to make it damp.

clue.text: Obstruct a view of an old city in the Middle East

definitions.text: of an old city in the Middle East

parts.note: to dam is to block a flow
a scene is a view or vista

explanation.surface: Something blocks the prospect of an ancient Middle Eastern city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Damascus in Syria, among the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

clue.text: Being on time, gets an order

parts.note: a man is a human being
a date is a fixed time

explanation.surface: Someone punctual is given a command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the time after the being in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An official instruction or authority to act is a command.

clue.text: Concentrated about the Oval

definitions.meaning: of writing or speech, condensed with words left out
relating to the shape of an ellipse

explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech omits words, as in an ellipsis; an ellipse is oval-shaped. THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.

clue.text: Draw together, opposing a plot

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
a tract is a plot or stretch of land

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a scene while resisting a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles or a purse-string that tighten and shrink are said to contract.

clue.text: The co-ordinator, giving a grin, rose unsteadily

indicators.note: the letters of a grin and rose wobble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smiling arranger got shakily to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges an event co-ordinates it.

clue.text: Sent back fit for discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word for fit is read upwards, sent back

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Someone was returned as fit to be released from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' suggests leaving the army; here it means to pour out in torrents.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that pours down heavily is said to stream or pour out.

clue.text: Leave a set in operation

parts.note: a band is a group or set of people
on means working, switched on

explanation.surface: A gang is told to quit while busy.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or forsake someone is to leave them behind.

clue.text: Subject of an article and a note

parts.note: the is the definite article
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An essay's topic is a newspaper piece plus a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a talk or composition is what it is about.

clue.text: A port some ships made — not all

indicators.note: only some of the letters in ships made not all are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Only some vessels completed the voyage to a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The port sits in 'made — not': mADE Not.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a harbour city in Yemen.

clue.text: Badly cut? There's a doctor round the corner

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go round the word for a corner, enclosing it

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: Someone with a nasty cut is told help is close by, a doctor just round the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hacked or torn about is mutilated, crushed or butchered.

clue.text: A bomb angered constituents

indicators.note: the parts of the word angered are taken apart and rebuilt into something new

explanation.surface: An explosive device has enraged the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like the voters of a constituency, but signals that the letters of ANGERED make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small explosive thrown by hand is a bomb of a particular kind.

clue.text: Increasing keenness

parts.note: reads as growing enthusiasm, but describes making a blade keener, honing it on a stone

explanation.definitionFit: Honing a knife makes its edge keener, and a sharp rise is a keen increase.

clue.text: Move slowly, though it produces some irritability

definitions.meaning: to inch or sidle forward gradually
being on this makes a person tense and twitchy, giving edginess

explanation.definitionFit: One inches along; also, being nervy is being 'on' it, as in the idiom for tension.

clue.text: The actors' entrances and exits

parts.note: reads as coming on and going off stage in a play, but means the literal doors to the theatre's backstage

explanation.definitionFit: Performers come and go through a theatre's back entrance, rather than walking onstage.

clue.text: He's retired before the small child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a tiny child

explanation.surface: A man has gone to bed before his little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests going to bed or leaving work; here it means withdrawn from the world, as a hermit is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse is a man who has withdrawn from society.

clue.text: The French people getting in late turned rude

indicators.note: the French article and the people get inside the reversed word
the word late is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the
men are people

explanation.surface: Late-arriving French people turned out to be impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives ETAL; 'getting in' places the other two pieces after its first letter. 'rude' is meant in its old sense of raw or primitive, not impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in its old sense of primitive or crude, raw like the basic forces of nature.

clue.text: Broke down in a test, and that's material

indicators.note: the letters of in a test collapse and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed during an exam, and that's the matter in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin satin-like fabric is a cloth, i.e. a material.

clue.text: Dissenter's strange exhaustion

indicators.note: the letters of the dissenter are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: the possessive 's gives no letters

explanation.surface: A nonconformist suffers an odd fatigue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out is fatigue, weariness.

clue.text: Hold tight!

parts.note: reads as a warning to grip on, as on a bus, but describes clasping someone close in your arms

explanation.definitionFit: A hug is holding a person tightly in your arms.

clue.text: Invalid correspondence?

parts.note: reads as void letters, but describes mail for a sick person laid up in bed

explanation.definitionFit: A post at a bed's corner, punning on letters delivered to a bedridden patient.

clue.text: Gun turned against a ringleader in uniform

indicators.note: the gun's name is turned round and read from the end back

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
the leading letter of the word ring

explanation.surface: A firearm is pointed at the uniformed head of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' means the first letter of RING, giving R; 'against' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even, unvarying and consistent throughout is uniform.

clue.text: What escapes from a lake, perhaps over a generation

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the next
the word lake is perhaps another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: Water escapes a lake, possibly over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is fluid escaping, so that which escapes is leaked matter.

clue.text: The team swank

explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team of players; 'side' is also pretentious airs, as in putting on side.

clue.text: : Turf award for a place

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
the OM, the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Grass is handed out as a prize for a location.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed for its wickedness is a place.

clue.text: Support the labourer used

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer who has been exploited is given backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods previously owned by someone else are used, not new.

clue.text: Duck take advantage of a watercourse

parts.note: a duck is a nil score, O
to use someone is to take advantage

explanation.surface: A bird exploits a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: OUSE is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in Yorkshire (and others in England) is a watercourse.

clue.text: The association's hit hard

definitions.meaning: a society; 's is short for is, linking to the second sense
to beat with a heavy stick

explanation.definitionFit: A society of members is a club; to bludgeon someone is to club them.

clue.text: Tiny amount of liquid from sink obstruction

parts.note: to drop is to fall or sink
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A little water comes from a blocked kitchen basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a kitchen basin but is the verb meaning fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drop or bead of fluid is a tiny quantity of it.

clue.text: The boards must accept gold for keeping

indicators.note: the theatre word must take in the gold, enclosing it

parts.note: the boards is a name for the theatrical stage
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A theatre is told to take gold into its safekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping things put away in a depot or warehouse is holding them in reserve.

clue.text: Postpone a dance for fly-by-nights?

definitions.meaning: a ball attended by night-flying insects

explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a project is to put it in storage like woollens; a party for night-flying insects would be their dance.

clue.text: Like certain collections, they're of some value

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
sets are groups of things that belong together

explanation.surface: Some collections, a remark goes, are worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: Property and possessions that have worth are the holdings of a business or person.
